comparator.name: Culturele antropologie en ontwikkelingssociologie
comparator.academicYear: Current 2026–27 curriculum and binding OER landing page; checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: Official current-student pages establish a 180-EC programme with 75 EC compulsory, 60 EC major choice and 45 EC profiling space. The compulsory part consists of six 7.5-EC first-year foundations and methods courses plus the four-stage 30-EC Bachelor Project (ethnographic methods, research design, fieldwork and thesis). Eight 7.5-EC major electives are required. No formal specialisation is imposed; the first eight electives in current official display order are instantiated neutrally, while the six-course profiling space remains open.

core: Cultural anthropology, social theory and comparative understanding of human societies
Culture, meaning, identity, belonging and everyday social life
Globalisation, migration, institutions, nationalism, conflict and power
Ethnographic fieldwork, qualitative methods, statistics and research writing
Diversity, inequality, exclusion and social development
Research ethics, reflexivity and representation of other perspectives
adjacent: Historical and material-cultural context for societies and identities
International relations, governance and transnational change
Human–environment relations and sustainability as fields of social change
questions: How can social problems be researched from people's own perspectives?
How do communities experience violence, security and conflict differently?
How do migration, identity and unequal power reshape societies?

alternatives.label: Cultural anthropology, society and qualitative research
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule combines comparative culture and society, theory, history, identity, qualitative methods, representation, power and advanced research.
alternatives.concept: A broad cultural-anthropology-inspired social-science programme centred on culture, meaning and social organisation, with historical comparison, qualitative research, power, conflict and representation.
progression: Introductory sociology, history and rhetoric precede advanced social theory, politics, representation and research. Qualitative methodology precedes advanced history research, and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Migration, identity and inequality
alternatives.labelReason: Direct interests in migration, cultural identity, power and inequality support a distinct route through gender, race, human rights, empires, Indigenous histories, social movements and exclusion.
alternatives.concept: A social and cultural programme focused on migration, identity formation, gender, race, rights, inequality and exclusion, supported by qualitative and historical research.
progression: Introductory sociology, history, rights and communication precede advanced social theory, race and representation, Indigenous histories and research. Qualitative methodology precedes the advanced research seminar, and every course is offered in its assigned term.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces rhetorical communication, world archaeology, political philosophy, EU politics and literary meaning with creative communication, media archaeology, youth resilience to extremism, Native American histories and environmental-justice movements. It therefore centres identity, exclusion and contested representation more directly.

alternatives.label: Globalisation, communities and social change
alternatives.labelReason: Direct interests in globalisation and local responses to change support a coherent route connecting social theory, governance, climate, sustainability, environmental justice and community research.
alternatives.concept: A social-science programme examining how communities respond to global political, environmental and cultural change through governance, social movements, communication and place-based research.
progression: Sustainability Essentials I precedes Sustainability Essentials II and Environmental Biogeochemistry. Introductory sociology and politics precede advanced governance, conflict, social theory and place-based sustainability research. Every course is offered in its assigned term.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces ten history, heritage, philosophy, law, language and literary courses with sustainability foundations, climate change, sustainability governance, climate communication, media and environment, ecosystems, environmental biogeochemistry, delta research and environmental-justice movements. The completed programme focuses global change through communities and human–environment relations.

selection.assessment: The broad closest match covers cultural anthropology's theory, comparative society and qualitative-research identity. Two direct programme-interest clusters support substantially distinct routes in migration/identity/inequality and globalisation/community change. Each contains a feasible 24-course schedule and production stops at the maximum of three alternatives.

notes.text: Utrecht combines a prescribed anthropology core with eight major electives and a compulsory 30-EC ethnographic Bachelor Project including fieldwork and thesis. UCR can construct strong culture-and-society pathways with qualitative research, identity, power and global-change content, but it does not reproduce the dedicated ethnographic fieldwork sequence; shared rows indicate substantive overlap rather than full equivalence.
